newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia faction takes rivals hostage on truce trip.
newsitem.headline: Liberia faction takes rivals hostage on truce trip.

text.p: A Liberian rebel faction has taken two rival commanders hostage while they were on a ceasefire monitoring mission to south east Liberia with U.N. officials and West African peacekeepers.

Members of the mission said in the capital Monrovia late on Tuesday that two generals of the National Patriotic Front of Liberia had been seized by the ethnic Krahn Liberia Peace Council as they left a U.N. helicopter in the town of Zwedru.
Peace Council fighters had robbed helicopter crew members and peacekeepers, taking cash, ammunition and communications equipment, they said.

Peacekeeping sources said that peacekeepers had taken in several leading members of the Peace Council in Monrovia and had won a pledge that the two hostages, generals John Tarnue and Francis Dolo, would be freed.
The two men are supporters of Charles Taylor, the man who launched the civil war in December 1989. The two factions have traded allegations of truce violations in the south east.

A Western diplomat who travelled with the truce monitoring team told reporters quick action was necessary to prevent the incident derailing Liberia's latest peace deal, which West African leaders brokered in Nigeria's capital Abuja in August.
The peace deal, backed up by the threat of individual sanctions against any faction leader undermining the process, envisages disarmament by January and elections in May.
The war has killed well over 150,000 people. The truce followed fighting that killed hundreds of people in Monrovia in April and May.
